items.title: Same RL sampling code on a DGX Spark and a rented H100 PCIe: H100 only 1.0x to 4.1x faster, not the 7.3x bandwidth ratio
items.summary: A team doing RL sampling on ByteDance's looped Ouro-1.4B timed one Python generation loop in the same NVIDIA container on a DGX Spark and an H100 PCIe: 4.1x with the stock cache code at batch 32, parity with their faster loop at 32, and 1.6x at batch 96, because a single host Python thread on the rented box kept the H100 34 to 50 percent busy. At batch 96 they estimate about $0.25 per thousand answers rented versus $0.04 to $0.12 on an owned Spark.

doubt.pushback: A forum reply notes the run used no CUDA Graphs or torch.compile, so the H100 was host-bound; the author agrees and plans to re-time with graphs, which would move the cost comparison toward renting.

items.title: SemiAnalysis: Kimi K3.1 Pro is first of 169 on Terminal-Bench 4.1 at 68.2% but 16th of 26 on private GDPx at 6.3%
items.summary: SemiAnalysis contrasts Kimi K3.1 Pro's top public Terminal-Bench 4.1 score with its rank on GDPx, its 206-task private agentic benchmark across 11 expert domains, where it trails Qwen 4 Max; its write-up calls K3.1 benchmaxxed on Terminal-Bench. Useful for anyone choosing an open model for agentic coding off public leaderboards.

doubt.pushback: Repliers ask whether both scores used the same harness and host (GDPx ran Kimi in Kimi Code via Fireworks; the official Terminal-Bench board with Claude Code puts K3.1 at 59.7%), and ask SemiAnalysis to publish GDPx task mix and contamination controls.

reception.summary: Most repliers read the gap as public-benchmark contamination and praise held-out evals; the specific critiques are harness and precision mismatch and a private benchmark nobody can audit. One reply points to a separate audit where K3.1 recalled hidden grading rules.

items.title: Open-source caregiver medication board runs LingSante 3.1 Flash at 1.51 bits per weight on one DGX Spark
items.summary: A builder released an MIT web app where a caregiver types a change in plain English and a local medical model rebuilds the pill schedule, flags drug interactions and lists questions for a pharmacist; it runs on a single DGX Spark with inclusionAI's LingSante 3.1 Flash quantized to 1.51 bpw at 28 to 30 tok/s. The only test shown is one synthetic patient with three planted interactions.

doubt.pushback: Single synthetic demo session (3 of 3 planted interactions flagged); no clinical evaluation, and the repo was created today.

items.title: Bare-metal 74 KB hypervisor puts a 2B LLM in Ring -1 to catch Linux kernel panics and live-patch guest RAM
items.summary: A Type-1 AMD SVM hypervisor written in NASM and libc-free C freezes Linux at a fatal Ring 0 fault, runs a GRPO-tuned MiniCPM5-2B on CPU to choose a patch, NOPs the faulting bytes through nested page tables and resumes the guest; the author reports 97.54% pass@1 on 122 unseen fault cases with no dangerous patches. Source is MIT on GitHub.

doubt.pushback: Repliers at the 23:23Z deep read questioned whether NOP-ing faulting bytes is a real fix and noted the test faults come from a purpose-built crash module; no new pushback on re-check.
